plan: OpenVibe.Help: a help centre generated from OpenVibe.Contracts at boot, search over it and over OpenVibe.Search, and support tickets that stay one conversation
summary: The help and support centre for every OpenVibe site. The help centre is generated at boot from openvibe-contracts (every product manifest and every service manifest's site block): one page per site, one page per question, each text quoted verbatim with its manifest named. /search searches those articles with a fixed explainable score and the network through OpenVibe.Search's public API (cached 5 minutes, degrading to the articles alone when it fails). A signed-in person opens a support ticket that stays one conversation — site, subject, message, an optional page URL stored as text and never fetched — sees only their own, and replies; staff by their Network role claim read the queue, filter it and set the state. Tickets live in PostgreSQL (migrations/0002_tickets.sql), writes made with the session cookie must be same-origin, and opening and answering are limited per caller. Sign-in is OpenVibe.Network (OAuth 2 + PKCE), the pages are server-rendered through the OpenVibe Frame and work without JavaScript, and the crawl artifacts cover every site and every question.
works: Help articles generated at boot from openvibe-contracts: 45 sites (22 live, 23 coming) and 20 questions across the 3 sites whose manifest carries an faq, quoted verbatim with provenance (manifest path, link back, read time)
/sites, /sites/:id (pillars as "what you can do", the FAQ as anchored articles, links to the site and its /updates) and /a/:site/:slug (one question per page, the question as the title)
Search: a fixed score over question/answer/site text for the help articles, plus OpenVibe.Search's public API in a second section; a 5-minute in-process cache, and a failure shown as a failure
Support tickets: create, list your own, one conversation per ticket, reply, staff queue with filters and open|waiting|solved, all in help_tickets and help_messages
Privacy: another person's ticket is a 404, anonymous is 401, an app token cannot act as a person, and a write with the session cookie must come from openvibe.help
Bodies are plain text, escaped with line breaks kept, capped at 10 000 characters; a page URL is stored as text and never fetched
Per-caller limits: help.ticket.create 6 a minute / 60 an hour, help.ticket.message 30 / 300
The API at /api/v1 with the problem+json error shape: sites, articles, tickets, staff
Crawl artifacts: a sitemap and llms-full.txt built from one page list (every site, every question), llms.txt listing the sites, JSON-LD for the home page, a site and a question
Sign-in with OpenVibe.Network (PKCE S256, server-side code exchange, httpOnly session cookies)
Truthful readiness (/api/ready: the database is required) and Prometheus metrics on loopback
Tests: the catalog against the manifests, escaping, search scoring with an OpenVibe.Search stand-in, and the whole ticket lifecycle including limits

Account export and deletion (ADR-033): the tickets a person opened and every message they wrote are exported to OpenVibe.Network on network.account.export_requested; on network.account.deleted their own tickets (and, by cascade, every message under them) are erased while a staff reply they left in someone else's ticket is anonymized, with the counts confirmed back; the two Events topics are subscribed at boot (server/identity/account-data.js)
notYet: A deployment: the service is not registered with OpenVibe.Services nor deployed by OpenVibe.Host
Its own service manifest and capability manifests in openvibe-contracts (contracts-service is help): CAPABILITIES in server/http/principal.js is empty until they exist
An email side to a ticket: today one conversation on the web, not yet the same thread by email
A "Report a problem" button on every other OpenVibe site (the product manifest's own launch note); a ticket can name a site but no site embeds the form yet

Answers drawn from the docs, wiki, blog and service status (the product manifest's description): today the articles are the sites' own manifests, and the network half of /search is what covers the rest
